title: Four quarters of qualification engineering revenue
body:
## The baseline: three thousand dollars of revenue

When POET Technologies filed its third-quarter 2024 interim report, the revenue line disclosed $3,685 — three thousand, six hundred and eighty-five dollars — of non-recurring engineering and product receipts. For a company whose market capitalisation had been moving in multiples of tens of millions on architectural enthusiasm for co-packaged optics, it was a deliberately legible number. Not a rounding artefact, not a revenue line that could be charitably read as early commercial traction. Three thousand dollars is a figure that places the entire platform thesis in crisp relief: POET is, as a matter of public disclosure record, a pre-commercial equity at this point in its operating history.

The number mattered less as an operating fact than as a framing device for what followed.

## The quarterly progression

The arc from Q3 2024 through Q4 2025 constitutes the entirety of POET's disclosed commercial revenue history as a photonics-interposer company. The sequential progression is the only operational story available from the public filings:

| Period | NRE & Product Revenue | Sequential Change |
|---|---|---|
| Q3 2024 | $3,685 | — |
| Q4 2024 | $29,032 | +688% |
| Q2 2025 | $268,469 | — |
| Q3 2025 | $298,434 | +11% |
| Q4 2025 | $341,202 | +14% |

*Sources: POET Technologies quarterly filings; [Q4 2025 earnings release](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-reports-fourth-quarter-2025-financial-results); [Q3 2025 earnings release](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-reports-third-quarter-2025-financial-results)*

From $3,685 to $341,202 across five quarters is a 93-fold increase. Framed that way, it reads as a growth story. Placed alongside the $18.08 million R&D expense line for FY2025, it reads as what it is: qualification engineering receipts, episodic and lumpy, from customers willing to pay POET to help them evaluate the Optical Interposer platform — not from customers placing volume production orders.

The distinction matters. NRE revenue is by definition non-recurring. It reflects an engineering relationship, often a time-gated evaluation, and it carries no guarantee of conversion to production. Each sequential disclosure — $29K, then a step to $268K in Q2 2025, then the more measured $298K and $341K as the second half progressed — was disclosing the stage of the customer qualification pipeline, not the arrival of commercial scale. Full-year 2025 revenue totalled approximately $1.2 million against an R&D spend of $18.08 million. POET's FY2025 revenue did not cover a single quarter of its own R&D run rate.

## Operating costs: the structural counter-narrative

While revenue moved from thousands to hundreds of thousands, operating expenses told a structurally divergent story. R&D expense for FY2025 reached $18.08 million, including $2.22 million of stock-based compensation. SG&A ran to $25.08 million, incorporating $3.89 million of stock-based compensation and $3.32 million of depreciation and amortisation. Non-cash operating costs across the consolidated statement approximated $35 million for the year.

The net loss for FY2025 was $62.96 million. Accumulated deficit at year-end 2025 stood at approximately $297 million — the cumulative equity consumed in pursuit of the platform thesis across the company's operating history.

The headcount and R&D scale-up during 2024 and 2025 was the structural explanation for the expense growth. As POET moved deeper into customer qualification cycles — which require engineering support, characterisation data, and sustained process iteration — the human and capital infrastructure costs expanded ahead of any corresponding revenue recognition. This is the standard pattern for pre-commercial photonics platforms: qualification is expensive before it converts, and the company bearing the qualification cost is POET, not the hyperscaler evaluating it.

## The $250 million financing: balance-sheet transformation as the defining event

The most consequential financial event in the period under review was not a revenue disclosure. It was the closing of a $250 million institutional equity financing from three undisclosed institutional buyers — the largest single capital transaction in POET's corporate history. The transaction expanded total assets from $69.7 million at December 2024 to $328.6 million at December 2025, a nearly fivefold balance-sheet expansion in a single fiscal year. Cash and short-term investments stood at $313.4 million at year-end 2025, [per the 20-F annual report filed in 2026](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/POET/20-f-poet-technologies-inc-files-annual-report-foreign-issuer-eeda6513f179.html).

Management's framing of the financing centred on runway and optionality: the proceeds, at the FY2025 cash operating loss rate of approximately $45 million per year, provide what amounts to a multi-year window to execute the Optical Interposer thesis through qualification and, in the optimistic scenario, into volume commitments from hyperscaler supply chains. Against the disclosed timeline of CPO deployment decisions expected in 2027 and 2028, the capital position is structurally adequate to be present when those decisions are made.

The financing also created the dilution overhang that will define POET's equity dynamics through the balance of the decade. Against 132.3 million common shares outstanding at December 2025, the company carries 5.79 million options and 37.36 million warrants — representing potential dilution of 28.35% on full exercise. The $135.6 million derivative warrant liability on the balance sheet is the non-cash mark-to-market recognition of that economic obligation, and it is one of the single most consequential line items in the consolidated financial statements.

## Sivers and the qualification engineering narrative

In September 2025, POET and Sivers Semiconductors announced a collaboration pairing Sivers Photonics' custom high-power indium phosphide DFB lasers with the POET Optical Interposer to develop external light source module candidates for co-packaged optics deployments. The announcement represented the most concretely disclosed strategic partnership in POET's public record at the snapshot date, and it arrived at a moment when the CPO architectural debate had intensified around Broadcom's Tomahawk roadmap disclosures and NVIDIA's evolving optical interconnect narrative.

POET shares were highly volatile through the 2024-2025 period — a consistent characteristic of small-cap equities that trade primarily on architectural news flows from companies an order of magnitude larger. Each Broadcom CPO announcement, each NVIDIA interconnect roadmap revision, each hyperscaler data-centre procurement signal moved POET's equity because none of those companies had named POET as a qualified supplier. The Sivers collaboration was notable precisely because it was a named, disclosed relationship with specific technical content — a concrete datapoint in the qualification engineering narrative rather than the ambient CPO enthusiasm that otherwise drove the stock.

Suresh Venkatesan, in framing POET's progress across the disclosure cadence, characterised the company's position consistently in terms of platform readiness and customer engagement depth rather than near-term revenue milestones — a defensible posture for a company at POET's development stage, and one entirely consistent with the financial record those same filings disclosed.

## What the cadence tells a sophisticated investor

Four quarters of sequential NRE and product revenue, read together, produce a coherent but bounded narrative. The sequential progression from $3,685 to $341,202 is real engineering progress — each step represents a deeper customer engagement, a further validated qualification milestone, an expanding base of relationships that might, under the right architectural conditions, convert into something larger. The balance-sheet expansion from $69.7 million to $328.6 million is equally real, and it materially changes the probability that POET will be present and funded when hyperscaler CPO qualification decisions reach their critical phase.

What the cadence does not produce — and what no quarterly filing in this sequence disclosed — is a commercial design-in announcement: the supply-chain commitment that would mark the transition from platform evaluation to volume production relationship. Each material headline through 2024-2025, from the Sivers collaboration to the $250 million financing, was a platform milestone, not an operating-company quarterly print.

At the snapshot date, POET's cumulative public revenue as a co-packaged optics interposer company totals approximately $1.2 million for FY2025. Its cash reserves stand at $313.4 million. The ratio of those two figures — roughly 260 times — is the most precise single expression of where this equity sits in its lifecycle: a platform-bet story in its fullest form, with the resources to wait for the thesis to resolve and no obligation from the current financial record to pretend it already has.
